Print method for 'sroc' objects

Source: R/print.sroc.R
print.sroc.Rd

This function prints the main results of reitsma.sroc (SROC curve) and hattori.tsroc (time-dependent SROC curve; one row for each time point), without considering publication bias: the number of studies, convergence of the optimizer, the SAUC, the summary sensitivity and specificity with their confidence intervals, and the estimates of \((\mu_1, \mu_2, \tau_1, \tau_2, \rho)\).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sroc'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted object returned by the function reitsma.sroc or hattori.tsroc.

digits

The number of decimal places of the results.

...

Other arguments in function print.default.

Value

x, invisibly. Called for the side effect of printing.

Details

Conv

"yes" indicates that nlminb converged (convergence = 0).

SAUC

The confidence interval is sauc.ci of the fitted object (calculated on the logit scale; see sauc).

Sens, Spec

\(\mathrm{plogis}(\mu_1)\) and \(\mathrm{plogis}(\mu_2)\); the confidence intervals are the Wald intervals of \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\), back-transformed.

tau1, tau2, rho

Between-study standard deviations (not variances) and correlation of the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity.

See summary.sroc for the standard errors and confidence intervals of all the parameters.

See also

reitsma.sroc, hattori.tsroc, summary.sroc, plot.sroc

Examples

## load data
data(IVD)

fit <- reitsma.sroc(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP, TN = TN, data = IVD)
fit
#> SROC curve: bivariate random-effects model (Reitsma et al., 2005)
#> Publication bias is not considered
#> 
#>   K Conv  SAUC         95% CI  Sens         95% CI  Spec         95% CI
#>  33  yes 0.874 [0.806, 0.920] 0.815 [0.757, 0.862] 0.861 [0.821, 0.893]
#> 
#> Estimates (tau1, tau2: between-study SDs; rho: correlation):
#>    mu1   mu2  tau1  tau2    rho
#>  1.484 1.824 0.597 0.826 -0.424
print(fit, digits = 4)
#> SROC curve: bivariate random-effects model (Reitsma et al., 2005)
#> Publication bias is not considered
#> 
#>   K Conv   SAUC           95% CI   Sens           95% CI   Spec
#>  33  yes 0.8736 [0.8058, 0.9201] 0.8152 [0.7570, 0.8620] 0.8610
#>            95% CI
#>  [0.8208, 0.8933]
#> 
#> Estimates (tau1, tau2: between-study SDs; rho: correlation):
#>     mu1    mu2   tau1   tau2     rho
#>  1.4840 1.8236 0.5974 0.8262 -0.4244
